title: India Launches Aarogya Setu 2.0, Unveils Sweeping Digital Health Overhaul
excerpt: Health Minister JP Nadda rolled out nearly a dozen interconnected platforms — from AI-powered health records and wearable integration to a WhatsApp chatbot and a unified drug registry — in India's most ambitious push yet to digitise healthcare for 1.4 billion people.
body:
India on Monday unveiled a sweeping overhaul of its digital health infrastructure, launching Aarogya Setu 2.0 alongside nearly a dozen interconnected platforms that aim to transform how healthcare is accessed, delivered, and managed across the country.

Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda launched the suite of digital initiatives at a flagship event in New Delhi that brought together state representatives, senior government officials, healthcare leaders, technology partners, and key stakeholders. The initiatives, developed under the National Health Authority (NHA) and the National Resource Centre for EHR Standards (NRCeS), represent what the government calls the next major milestone in building a connected, interoperable healthcare ecosystem for India's 1.4 billion people.

## Aarogya Setu Reborn

The centrepiece of the launch is Aarogya Setu 2.0, a comprehensive Personal Health Record (PHR) application that builds on the trust and reach the original app established during the COVID-19 pandemic. But where the original was primarily a contact-tracing tool, the revamped version is designed as a gateway to India's entire digital health stack.

The new app enables creation and management of ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) identifiers, access to and consent-based sharing of digital health records, AI-powered health insights and smart health reports, and integration with wearable devices such as fitness trackers and smartwatches. It also offers OPD registration through "Scan & Register," hospital payments through "Scan & Pay," medication reminders, and family health management — all within a single platform.

Practical features include discovery of nearby healthcare facilities, doctors, ambulance services, blood banks with real-time availability, and Jan Aushadhi Kendras (affordable medicine centres). Beneficiaries of the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) can also access their insurance wallet and policy details through the app.

## Beyond the App: A Health Data Revolution

The launch extended well beyond a single application. The suite of tools unveiled on Monday includes:

**Ayushman Sarathi WhatsApp Chatbot** — a conversational interface allowing citizens to access health services through India's most widely used messaging platform, bringing digital health to users who may not download a dedicated app.

**National Health Claims Exchange (NHCX)** — a platform enabling seamless, standardised exchange of health insurance claims between hospitals, insurers, and third-party administrators. It is expected to significantly reduce the time and paperwork involved in cashless hospitalisation and claims settlement.

**Unified Health Interface (UHI)** — an open network with common technical standards that allows patients and healthcare providers to connect across different digital platforms without being locked into any single application. When a citizen uses a UHI-enabled app to search for a health service, the request is routed through a gateway to registered providers, enabling discovery, booking, and fulfilment through a common protocol.

**Drug Registry** — a unified, standardised digital platform for drug-related information, developed in collaboration with the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO). Leveraging international standards such as SNOMED CT, it serves as a single source of truth for medicines in India, enabling consistent identification and exchange of drug data across healthcare systems.

**e-Sushrut Clinic** — a provider-focused solution designed to digitise clinical workflows in small and medium healthcare facilities.

Additional tools launched include the Insurance Plan FHIR Object Creator, Common LOINC Codes for India (CLCI), and the Bharat Health Terminology Service (BHTS) — foundational standards that enable the various platforms to communicate using a shared digital language.

## A High-Profile Audience

The event underscored the government's commitment to digital health as a policy priority. In addition to Minister Nadda, attendees included Minister of State for Health Prataprao Jadhav, Minister of State Anupriya Patel, NITI Aayog Member (Health) Dr M. Srinivas, Tripura Chief Minister Dr Manik Saha, Madhya Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Rajendra Shukla, and Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak. Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava, ICMR Director General Dr Rajiv Bahl, and NHA CEO Dr Sunil Kumar Barnwal also participated.

## What This Means for the Indian Diaspora

For the millions of NRIs managing their parents' and family members' healthcare from abroad, these initiatives address a longstanding pain point. The ABHA system creates a portable, consent-based health identity that can store medical records digitally, potentially allowing NRIs to review their family members' health data remotely — from prescriptions and lab results to hospital discharge summaries.

The wearable device integration is particularly relevant for tech-savvy diaspora members who have equipped their parents with fitness trackers or smartwatches. Health data from these devices can now feed into a centralised personal health record, giving families a more complete picture of wellness indicators.

The Unified Health Interface could eventually make telemedicine more accessible for cross-border consultations. And for NRIs who visit India and need medical care, the Scan & Register and Scan & Pay features simplify what has traditionally been a paper-heavy, queue-intensive hospital experience.

The Drug Registry, with its standardised medication information, could also prove useful for diaspora families coordinating medication management across countries — ensuring that prescriptions and drug names are clearly mapped to international standards.

India's digital health push comes as the country's broader digital public infrastructure story, from UPI to Aadhaar, continues to draw international attention. With the healthcare stack now moving toward similar interoperability and scale, the government is betting that the same approach can transform one of the world's most complex and fragmented healthcare systems.
